venues.name: Every Neighborhood Partnership
venues.one_liner: Fresno nonprofit that explicitly opens its building to other nonprofits and community groups, with a meeting area for up to 100 people.
signals: large meeting area up to 100 people
explicitly offers space to nonprofits and community groups
full kitchen on site
published facility-use request form
central Fresno, 1631 N Van Ness Ave
venues.suggested_first_move: Submit the facility-use request form for Saturday 31 Oct 2026, asking for a 8am-7pm hold and confirming wifi, power, and cost in the same message.
venues.notes: Best $0-budget fit found: capacity (100) clears the 60-person cap with room for mentors and judges, and the org's own page states it opened the building specifically so nonprofits could stop struggling to find affordable venues. Two things are NOT published and must be asked on first contact: the fee (if any) and weekend availability. No individual staff member is named on the page, so the request form is the only documented route.

venues.name: Fresno Ideaworks
venues.one_liner: All-volunteer 501(c)(3) community makerspace in the historic Crown Plunge building downtown, with a dedicated tech classroom/hackerspace.
signals: downtown Fresno, 1730 H Street
dedicated tech classroom / hackerspace area
runs public classes and monthly Art Hop events
active class calendar through September 2026
501(c)(3), operating since 2013, owns its building
venues.warm_path: Their CoderDojo youth-coding program and tech classroom mean they already host software teaching — lead with that, not with 'we need a room'.
venues.suggested_first_move: Email info@fresnoideaworks.org (559-833-4332) asking whether the tech classroom plus main floor can host 60 people on Sat 31 Oct 2026, and what a partner/member rate looks like.
venues.notes: Organization is unambiguously live: the site shows classes scheduled into August and September 2026 and current membership signup. What I could NOT verify is seated capacity — no square footage or occupancy figure is published on their site, and a makerspace floorplan (welding, ceramics, woodshop) may not seat 60 people at tables. Treat capacity as an open question on the call. Board roster is published but undated; see mentor entry for Ryan Madron.

venues.name: Fresno Unified School District facilities (via Facilitron)
venues.one_liner: District-wide Civic Center Act rentals — classrooms, theaters, gyms and more at Fresno high schools — bookable online through Facilitron.
signals: live online booking system for the district
classrooms, theaters, gyms available to community groups
nine named Fresno high schools listed
Civic Center Act permits weekend and holiday use
clustered classrooms suit a hackathon's breakout-team shape
venues.warm_path: Fresno Unified already takes tech-education money locally (Amazon funded robotics clubs there), so the district has a live interest in student-facing tech events.
venues.suggested_first_move: Create a Facilitron requester account and price a Saturday booking at two schools (e.g. Fresno High, Sunnyside High) to see the real nonprofit rate before committing.
venues.notes: Genuinely weekend-accessible, but not free: the district requires a Commercial General Liability policy of at least $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate with the district named as additional insured, plus a $50 cancellation fee. Against a $0 budget the insurance requirement alone may be disqualifying unless a partner org lends its policy. Specific room capacities and rates are not published on the platform's landing page.

venues.name: Fresno County Public Library — Woodward Park and Sunnyside branch meeting rooms
venues.one_liner: County library branches whose published policy lists free meeting rooms, including rooms rated for 140 and 70 people.
signals: no charge during open hours
policy document lists Woodward Park at 140 and Sunnyside at 70
nonprofits and community groups may reserve
Woodward Park open Saturdays 9am-5pm
online reservation system (LibCal)
venues.suggested_first_move: Call (559) 600-7323 and ask one question first: is the Woodward Park meeting room rated for 140 still bookable, and until what time on a Saturday.
venues.notes: Downgraded to low on purpose — the sources contradict each other. The library's own meeting-room policy document lists Woodward Park Meeting Room at 140 and Sunnyside at 70, but the Woodward Park branch page describes only a 6-person conference room and a 2-person study room, and the LibCal booking system's capacity filters top out around 50. Two further constraints even if a large room exists: Saturday hours end at 5pm, which truncates an all-day event, and the policy forbids charging admission or soliciting donations, which can conflict with sponsor tabling. Real, free, and worth one phone call — but do not build the plan on it.

venues.name: Fresno State campus space (Student Recreation Center / Peters Educational Center)
venues.one_liner: Campus venue path — a 300-seat auditorium and the Lyles Center sit in the Student Recreation Center — reachable only through a campus co-sponsor.
signals: 300-seat Peters Educational Center auditorium
Lyles Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship in the same building
50,000+ sq ft facility, campus 25Live scheduling system
student volunteer pipeline on site
venues.warm_path: Fresno State's Computer Science department and the Lyles Center are both plausible co-sponsors, and Corporate & Foundation Relations (see sponsors) is the same institution.
venues.suggested_first_move: Do not call facilities first. Ask the CS department or Lyles Center to co-host, then let them book the room through campus scheduling (559-278-2491).
venues.notes: Listed as a path, not a booking. Verification found a hard barrier: Fresno State Library's space policy states spaces cannot be reserved by organizations or individuals not affiliated with Fresno State, and the SRC auditorium page directs on-campus departments to campus scheduling. So an outside organizer cannot book this directly — the lead is only live if a campus partner fronts it. Rates are not published anywhere I could load.

sponsors.name: Central Valley Community Foundation
sponsors.one_liner: Fresno-based community foundation running the region's flagship workforce and inclusive-economy programs.
signals: foundation with documented workforce/economic-development grantmaking
Fresno DRIVE: $4.2B, 14 initiatives, human-capital pillar
F3 (Farms Food Future) and Sierra San Joaquin Jobs (S2J2)
$200M+ raised since 2017, 900+ grants in the past decade
based in Fresno at 1260 Fulton Street
sponsors.warm_path: Pitch into the Fresno DRIVE human-capital pillar rather than as a generic event — DRIVE explicitly counts workers trained as its outcome.
sponsors.suggested_first_move: Email info@centralvalleycf.org (559-226-5600) referencing the DRIVE human-capital pillar and ask for 20 minutes; use the 'Partner With Us' route on the same page.
sponsors.notes: Clears the revenue gate as a foundation with named workforce and economic-development programs, and it is the single best door-opener in this file — CVCF convenes roughly 150 organizations through DRIVE, so one meeting is a map of the rest of the city. Downgraded from high to med by the verification pass: the community-impact page describes convening and advocacy ('advocates for $4.2B of investment') more than it documents an open grant cycle, states no application process, eligibility, or deadline for outside organizations, and its clearest funding evidence is indirect (nearly $5M in small-business loans via PRO Neighborhoods). Treat as a relationship and referral lead, not an application lead.

sponsors.name: Educational Employees Credit Union (EECU)

documented event sponsorships (Bridge2College, Latino Student Success Conference)
education is its stated giving focus
2026 Fresno Compact Business-Education Partnership Award
financial-wellness workshops delivered in schools
sponsors.warm_path: Their giving is education-shaped. Frame the hackathon as workforce/skills for local students and nonprofit staff, not as a tech conference.
sponsors.suggested_first_move: Use the Contact Us form on their community page to ask who handles event sponsorship requests and what the lead time is — no public sponsorship form exists.
sponsors.notes: Gate note: a credit union is member-owned rather than for-profit, so I am admitting it on scale and demonstrated cash sponsorship rather than on the letter of the for-profit test — third-party 990 data puts assets at roughly $4.7B. That asset figure is NOT on EECU's own pages, which is why confidence is med rather than high. Their own page confirms the sponsorship behavior and the education focus; it does not confirm headquarters address or size.

sponsors.name: Granville Homes
sponsors.one_liner: Fresno-headquartered homebuilder with a formal foundation and an open community-sponsorship application.
signals: headquartered in Fresno, 1306 W Herndon Ave

online Community Sponsorship application portal
~$35M revenue / ~104 employees (third-party data) clears the $5M gate
sponsors.warm_path: Home of Hope proceeds go to Fresno nonprofits — several of your likely attendees are probably already recipients, which is a real introduction if you find one.
sponsors.suggested_first_move: Submit the Community Sponsorship application on the philanthropy page, and name which local nonprofits are attending.
sponsors.notes: One of only a few Fresno companies with a published, self-serve route to ask for money — that matters more than size for a cold organizer. Verification confirmed the live application link and the Fresno HQ address on the page itself. Two caveats it does NOT state: any eligibility criteria, deadline, or decision timeline for the sponsorship application; and the '60+ organizations assisted' figure is dated 2019, so current giving volume is unknown. Giving is framed around food/shelter/healthcare/education, so the ask should be education/workforce, not innovation. Revenue and headcount come from third-party business data, not their own site.

sponsors.name: Community West Bank (Community West Bancshares, NASDAQ: CWBC)

sponsors.notes: Clears the gate cleanly (public company, Fresno HQ, ~$5B assets). Formerly Central Valley Community Bancorp; the rename followed a 2024 merger, so older references to 'CVCB' are the same institution — worth knowing so you don't pitch them twice. No named community-giving program is published, so the first call is a routing call.

sponsors.notes: Passes the gate as a foundation with a documented workforce/STEM program. The blocker is procedural and stated plainly on their page: 'we do not accept unsolicited grant requests by email.' So this is a relationship lead, not an application lead, and it is unlikely to convert inside a 13-week runway. Scored for quality, flagged for timing.

sponsors.notes: Per the revenue gate, the university's corporate-engagement/foundation arm is the sponsorable entity — a professor is not. This office may also route you to corporate partners rather than write a check itself, which is arguably more valuable in a cold city. Title and contact details verified on the university's own page; I have not confirmed the person is still in post beyond that page.

First, DevFest Fresno traditionally runs in the fall, so 31 Oct 2026 may collide with their own event; ask early. Second, the chapter page showed NO upcoming events at the time of checking, with the most recent past event in June 2026 — activity may be seasonal, but confirm the chapter is currently running before depending on it.

established Community Action Agency
existing workforce-training infrastructure

The value here is audience and problem statements — 35+ frontline programs is a deep well of real nonprofit workflows for teams to build against.

in_kind_partners.notes: Deliberately placed in-kind rather than sponsors. It is a government agency, but its money is WIOA-restricted and moves through competitive RFPs and contracts, not event sponsorships — asking for a check would burn the relationship and waste your runway. Ask instead for participant recruitment and employer introductions. No executive director is named on the page I loaded.

verification_notes: Method: sourcing and verification were run as separate passes. Every URL in this file was fetched and read; nothing is included on the strength of a search-result snippet alone. Where a fact came only from a search summary or third-party aggregator (revenue figures, asset totals), it is labelled as such in the lead's notes and the confidence is capped at med.

SECOND-PASS RESULT: every source_url was re-requested and all 26 unique URLs returned HTTP 200. Four highest-stakes leads were then re-fetched with adversarial prompts. Every Neighborhood Partnership held (the page literally states 'accommodates up to 100 people' and 'open the doors of our new building to other nonprofits and community groups', Fresno address in footer, blog activity June-July 2026). Granville Homes held (live application link, Fresno HQ address on page). The GDG Fresno organizer roster held unchanged (all three organizers, 823 members, no upcoming events, no emails published). Central Valley Community Foundation did NOT fully hold and was downgraded from high to med — see its notes.

DROPPED — Bitwise Industries: the obvious 'Fresno tech' answer and completely dead. Filed Chapter 7 on 29 June 2023 listing $252.03M in liabilities after furloughing ~900 employees; co-founders removed by the board. Any lead list for Fresno that includes Bitwise is a list nobody verified.

DROPPED — Lyons Magnus: $617M revenue and reportedly Fresno-headquartered, which would have made it a strong sponsor, but its own homepage does not state a headquarters location and its /contact/ page returned 404. No page I could load backs the Fresno claim, so it is out under sourced-or-omitted.

DROPPED — Fresno First Bank: a plausible Fresno-headquartered bank prospect; fresnofirstbank.com returned HTTP 403 and I could not load any page of its own to confirm it currently operates under that name. Dropped rather than cited unread.

DROPPED — Table Mountain Rancheria: considered as a government/tribal sponsor. Its community page describes partnerships and a general commitment but names no grant program, focus areas, application process, or amounts. Fails the 'government agency ONLY with a specific named grant program' gate. Dropped rather than softened.

DROPPED — James B. McClatchy Foundation: a real, well-funded Fresno foundation, but its documented programs are English Learners, First Amendment/journalism, arts and civic education — no tech or workforce program — and it accepts proposals by invitation only. Fails the foundation gate on both counts.

DROPPED — Valley Children's Healthcare Foundation: its published corporate route is cause marketing and gala sponsorship benefiting the hospital, not sponsorship of third-party community events, and no corporate-partnership contact is named on the page. Also Madera, not Fresno. Not worth an organizer's limited runway.
DROPPED — GDG on Campus, CSU Fresno: the student chapter page returned HTTP 404, so I could not confirm the chapter currently exists. The city chapter (GDG Fresno) is verified and retained.

DOWNGRADED — Fresno County Public Library: the library's own meeting-room policy lists Woodward Park at 140 and Sunnyside at 70 seats, free of charge, but the Woodward Park branch page describes only a 6-person conference room and the LibCal booking system's capacity filters top out near 50. Sources contradict each other on the central claim, so confidence is low and the lead carries the contradiction in its notes rather than picking the flattering number.

DOWNGRADED — Fresno State campus space: kept only as a co-sponsor path, not a booking. The library's space policy explicitly bars reservations by organizations not affiliated with Fresno State, and the 300-seat auditorium is routed through on-campus departments. An outside organizer cannot book campus space directly.

RECLASSIFIED — Fresno Economic Opportunities Commission: initially a sponsor candidate; its own sponsorship page states it is not currently accepting sponsorship requests. Moved to in-kind with a partner ask.

RECLASSIFIED — Fresno Regional Workforce Development Board: a government agency administering named WIOA programs, so it arguably clears the gate, but its funds move through competitive RFPs rather than event sponsorship. Moved to in-kind so nobody spends runway asking it for a check.
RECLASSIFIED — Community Health System: largest employer in the Central Valley, but a nonprofit health system with no named grant or sponsorship program on any page I loaded. In-kind, not sponsor.

GATE EXCEPTIONS, stated openly: two sponsors are admitted on grounds other than the for-profit $5M test. EECU is a member-owned credit union admitted on scale (~$4.7B assets per third-party 990 data) plus a demonstrated record of cash event sponsorship. Kaiser Permanente is a nonprofit health system admitted on a documented, named sponsorship program that explicitly covers education and workforce development. Both are flagged in their notes; neither figure appears on the organization's own pages.

TIME-CRITICAL: Kaiser Permanente requires sponsorship requests at least 3 months before the event. With the event on 31 Oct 2026 and research dated 1 Aug 2026 (91 days out), this lead expires within days of this file being written.

Venue reality check against a $0 budget: of five venue leads, only Every Neighborhood Partnership combines a published capacity above the 60-person cap with an explicit invitation to nonprofits. Fresno Unified via Facilitron requires $1M/$2M liability insurance naming the district as additional insured. The library is free but forbids soliciting donations and closes at 5pm Saturday. Fresno State needs a campus co-sponsor. Ideaworks publishes no capacity figure.

The event date moved to Saturday 7 November 2026 during this research pass. 31 October was verified as a Saturday but is Halloween, which competes for volunteer and attendee attention; 7 November is a Saturday, 97 days out, and clear of holidays. Library Saturday hours, the Civic Center Act weekend provision, and weekend venue access all still apply.

No individuals were invented. Every named person comes from the employing or hosting organization's own web page: the GDG Fresno chapter organizer list, the Fresno State CS faculty directory, the Fresno State Advancement staff listing, the Kaiser Permanente Fresno service-area contacts, and the Fresno Ideaworks board page. Where an organization published no individual (Every Neighborhood Partnership, Lyles Center, Valley Community SBDC, FRWDB, Fresno EOC), the organization is listed and the absence of a named contact is stated rather than filled in.
No one was contacted. No emails sent, no forms submitted, no reservations requested. Every 'first move' is an action for the organizer, not something already done.

Schema note for the assembler: in_kind_partners entries use type 'partner', which extends the data contract's venue|sponsor|mentor enum. Labelling a partner as a 'sponsor' would undercut the rule that in-kind orgs never receive a cash ask. render() does not validate type, so this renders correctly today, but the contract should be updated to include it.
warnings: Mentors: 9 named individuals are sourced, above the 6 done-signal, but the bench is academically weighted. Only 3 (the GDG Fresno organizers) are hands-on industry practitioners of the mid-career profile mentors should have; 5 are Fresno State faculty and 1 is a makerspace board officer whose current role could not be confirmed. If GDG Fresno declines, the practitioner bench collapses to zero and this section is effectively thin.

Sponsors: 10 prospects clear the revenue gate, exactly at the done-signal, but only 4 publish a self-serve route to ask for money (Granville Homes' application portal, Kaiser Permanente's named contacts, Fresno State's named director, and CVCF's partner route). The rest require finding the right person by phone first, and PG&E states outright that it does not accept unsolicited requests. Plan for a low conversion rate inside 13 weeks.

Venues: 5 leads clear the 3 done-signal, but only 1 (Every Neighborhood Partnership) is both confirmed above 60 capacity and explicitly open to nonprofits. Every other venue carries a cost, access, capacity, or hours caveat documented in its notes. Do not treat this section as five interchangeable options.

Two leads carry unresolved source contradictions, kept visible rather than resolved by guessing: Fresno County Public Library capacity (policy document vs branch page vs booking system) and the current president of Fresno Ideaworks (undated board page vs a public interview naming someone else).

Zero warm paths are real introductions. Nobody on this team has a relationship in Fresno, and no lead in this file came from one. Every 'warm_path' is an inferred route from published information, not a person who will vouch for you. The first ten outreach attempts will be cold.

Verification confirms these organizations exist, operate, and are located in or near Fresno. It does NOT confirm availability on 31 Oct 2026, willingness to participate, current budget, or that any named individual still holds their role. No lead here has been contacted.
